title: JDK 27 G1/Parallel/Serial GC changes
excerpt: Since the OpenJDK 27 release is on the horizon I thought it would be time to discuss interesting changes in OpenJDK’s stop-the-world collectors in the HotSpot VM once more.
content_html:
Since the OpenJDK 27 release is on the horizon I thought it would be time to discuss interesting changes in OpenJDK’s stop-the-world collectors in the HotSpot VM once more.

The complete list of resolved/closed changes for the GC subcomponent for JDK 27 is here, containing around 350 changes in total.

This raw count aligns with last release; similar to then, these numbers may be a bit inflated because of a fairly unusual number of refactorings and cleanups in the GC code.

One particular area in the STW collector area has been replacing our idiom to indicate cross-thread shared variables, from using volatile and appropriate AtomicAccess methods on them to using Atomic<T> introduced in JDK-8367013 to make their use more explicit. Other notable refactorings include G1 state machine cleanups (including some very very old ones) and other code improvements. These make up around half of the changes.

Roughly another 35% of changes deal with bug fixes and general correctness and robustness improvements. The remainder is about new or materially revised behavior and features for HotSpot’s STW collectors - and this is the part this post will dig down further now :)

Mixed in with these changes was infrastructure work for JEP 401: Value Objects (Preview), like adapting object iterators and eager reclaim for value objects.

The most impactful change in this release has probably been JEP 523: Make G1 the Default Garbage Collector in All Environments. G1 is now the default collector if one does not specify any garbage collection algorithm explicitly on the command line. No exceptions, no Serial GC in any case by default (that is, unless G1 is not included in your distribution of OpenJDK :)). We thought that G1 fit the bill of a default collector nicely, and selecting something else depending on arcane environmental conditions was more of a burden than an advantage. Throughput, footprint and latency profile were step-by-step closing in on Serial GC in the applications it was still better, particularly in the past few releases, so we felt it was about time to flip the switch.

One may still select Serial GC with the -XX:+UseSerialGC option if you observe notable differences to get pure, unchanged Serial GC. There obviously are some cases where for your application profile Serial GC is the better choice - G1 is not the best everywhere, but we think it is certainly the best to start off with.

Next to that change, there are a few others:

  • G1 no longer resizes the heap after Full GC based on the (arbitrary) -XX:MinHeapFreeRatio and -XX:MaxHeapFreeRatio percentages, that is, their default values have been set so that they do not impact regular, other heuristics based sizing (e.g. garbage collector CPU usage relative to the application’s CPU usage). JDK-8238686 set their defaults to 0 and 100 percent respectively, from 40 and 70 respectively.

    The original defaults caused this heuristic and others like the CPU usage based one to fight each other, resulting in unnecessary Java heap size modifications, causing performance issues when a full heap garbage collection shrunk the heap and then the other heuristics almost immediately undid these changes.

    Other than that, these flags’ functionality is preserved.

  • Adaptive start of concurrent marking has been improved to be more resistant to adverse conditions that previously caused unnecessary continuous concurrent work (JDK-8379846, JDK-8381006).

  • Previously, humongous objects that actually could be reclaimed were inadvertently held live by weak references (e.g. java.lang.ref.Reference instances), fixed with JDK-8378331 and JDK-8378336.

  • Minor observable changes include that the G1 Cleanup pauses do not update MemoryPoolMXBean.getCollectionUsage() as they do not change the Java heap in JDK-8386332. JDK-8373894 where previously garbage collections that could not find enough space to copy to were not counted in garbage collector CPU usage. Including them improves heap-sizing decisions.

Parallel GC

Parallel GC had some notable bug fixes that may improve performance:

  • The adaptive tenuring threshold determines how many young collections an object may stay within the young generation. Previously, the threshold tended to only increase, but very rarely decrease. This means such a persistently high threshold could leave older objects taking much of the survivor space, forcing younger objects to be promoted prematurely when it filled up. With JDK-8380590, the threshold can decrease as well, promoting longer-lived objects sooner and preserving younger objects that are likely to die shortly in the young generation.

  • Parallel GC now correctly expands the Java heap when repeated large allocations cause thousands of Full GCs while the Java heap did not grow even if there was enough headroom JDK-8377561.

Serial GC

No notable Serial GC specific changes - except for not being the default collector in some cases anymore.

All Collectors

There were a few interesting changes to all collectors:

  • TLAB sizing now better handles applications that create many short-lived, lightly allocating threads. This avoids oversizing TLABs that result in a large amount of waste, increasing the number of collections JDK-8381834.

  • JDK-8372348 improves string deduplication logging and JFR events. Logging adds “new unknown” strings and gives more meaningful aggregate byte counts.

What’s next

Our focus remains on Automatic Heap Sizing, improving control of various aspects of memory management so that G1 can respond more intelligently to external conditions and user intent.

Thanks go to…

… as usual to everyone that contributed to another JDK release. Finally, with some major refactorings (Atomic<T>) complete, more time is available for other items. Looking forward seeing you in the next - maybe even bigger - release :)

Thomas

blocks.html_en: The adaptive tenuring threshold determines how many young collections an object may stay within the young generation. Previously, the threshold tended to only increase, but very rarely decrease. This means such a persistently high threshold could leave older objects taking much of the survivor space, forcing younger objects to be promoted prematurely when it filled up. content_html_zh:
由于 OpenJDK 27 版本即将发布，我认为是时候再次讨论 HotSpot VM 中 OpenJDK 的 stop-the-world 收集器的有趣变化了。

JDK 27 的 GC 子组件已解决/已关闭更改的完整列表位于此处，总共包含约 350 个更改。

此原始计数与上次版本一致；与当时类似，这些数字可能有点夸大，因为 GC 代码中的重构和清理次数相当不寻常。

STW 收集器区域中的一个特定区域已经取代了我们的习惯用法来指示跨线程共享变量，从使用 volatile 和适当的 AtomicAccess 方法到使用 JDK-8367013 中引入的 Atomic<T> 以使它们的使用更加明确。 其他值得注意的重构包括 G1 状态机清理（包括一些非常非常旧的状态机）和其他代码改进。 这些约占变化的一半。

大约另外 35% 的更改涉及错误修复以及一般正确性和稳健性改进。 其余部分是关于 HotSpot 的 STW 收集器的新的或重大修改的行为和功能 - 这是本文现在将进一步深入探讨的部分:)

与这些更改混合在一起的是 JEP 401：值对象（预览版）的基础设施工作，例如调整对象迭代器和对值对象的热切回收。

此版本中最有影响力的更改可能是 JEP 523：使 G1 成为所有环境中的默认垃圾收集器。 如果没有在命令行上显式指定任何垃圾收集算法，G1 现在是默认收集器。 没有例外，默认情况下任何情况下都没有串行 GC（也就是说，除非 G1 未包含在您的 OpenJDK 发行版中:)）。 我们认为 G1 非常适合默认收集器的要求，而根据神秘的环境条件选择其他东西更多的是一种负担，而不是一种优势。 在应用程序中，吞吐量、占用空间和延迟配置文件逐步接近串行 GC，但它仍然更好，特别是在过去的几个版本中，因此我们认为是时候进行转换了。

如果您观察到获得纯粹的、未更改的串行 GC 的显着差异，仍然可以选择带有 -XX:+UseSerialGC 选项的串行 GC。 显然，在某些情况下，对于您的应用程序配置文件，串行 GC 是更好的选择 - G1 并不是在所有地方都是最好的，但我们认为它肯定是最好的开始。

除了该更改之外，还有其他一些更改：

  • G1 不再根据（任意）-XX:MinHeapFreeRatio 和 -XX:MaxHeapFreeRatio 百分比在 Full GC 后调整堆大小，也就是说，它们的默认值已设置，以便它们不会影响常规的、其他基于启发式的大小调整（例如，垃圾收集器 CPU 使用率相对于应用程序的 CPU 使用率）。 JDK-8238686 将它们的默认值分别从 40% 和 70% 设置为 0% 和 100%。 最初的默认设置导致这种启发式方法和其他启发式方法（例如基于 CPU 使用率的启发式方法）互相争斗，导致不必要的 Java 堆大小修改，从而在完整堆垃圾收集缩小堆时导致性能问题，然后其他启发式方法几乎立即撤消这些更改。 除此之外，这些标志的功能被保留。
  • 并发标记的自适应启动已得到改进，可以更好地抵抗先前导致不必要的连续并发工作的不利条件（JDK-8379846、JDK-8381006）。
  • 以前，实际上可以回收的巨大对象会无意中被弱引用（例如 java.lang.ref.Reference 实例）保留，已使用 JDK-8378331 和 JDK-8378336 进行了修复。
  • 可观察到的细微更改包括 G1 清理暂停不会更新 MemoryPoolMXBean.getCollectionUsage()，因为它们不会更改 JDK-8386332 中的 Java 堆。 JDK-8373894，以前无法找到足够空间进行复制的垃圾收集不计入垃圾收集器 CPU 使用率。 包含它们可以改善堆大小决策。

并行气相色谱

并行 GC 修复了一些值得注意的错误，可以提高性能：

  • 自适应保有阈值确定对象可以保留在年轻代中的多少个年轻集合。 此前，门槛只会增加，很少会减少。 这意味着如此持续高的阈值可能会使较旧的对象占用大部分幸存者空间，迫使较年轻的对象在填满时过早地升级。 使用 JDK-8380590，阈值也可以降低，更快地提升寿命较长的对象，并保留可能在年轻代中很快消亡的年轻对象。
  • 现在，当重复的大型分配导致数千次 Full GC 时，并行 GC 可以正确扩展 Java 堆，而即使有足够的空间 JDK-8377561，Java 堆也不会增长。

串行GC

没有显着的串行 GC 特定变化 - 除了在某些情况下不再成为默认收集器之外。

所有收藏家

所有收藏家都发生了一些有趣的变化：

  • TLAB 大小调整现在可以更好地处理创建许多短期、少量分配线程的应用程序。 这避免了 TLAB 过大导致大量浪费，增加集合数量 JDK-8381834。
  • JDK-8372348 改进了字符串重复数据删除日志记录和 JFR 事件。 日志记录添加了“新的未知”字符串，并提供了更有意义的聚合字节计数。

接下来是什么

我们的重点仍然是自动堆大小调整，改进对内存管理各个方面的控制，以便 G1 可以更智能地响应外部条件和用户意图。

谢谢去…

… 像往常一样，对每个为另一个 JDK 版本做出贡献的人来说。 最后，随着一些主要重构 (Atomic<T>) 的完成，有更多时间可用于其他项目。 期待在下一个版本中见到您 - 也许甚至更大 - 版本:)

托马斯
